messages:
olivia: Quick heads-up — did a springboard-v1 bringup with int8 quant across us-east / us-west / eu-west. Compared H100 (pinned) vs A100 (burst) with two routing configs: direct-pop and edge-mux. p50 looks fine, but p95 in eu-west jumps ~60-90ms under edge-mux. attaching raw numbers below.

samir: Can you paste the p50/p95 table and what workload (seq len / batch) you used?

olivia: Test config: seq=512, static batch=1 (simulating interactive), 30k requests steady over 20m, prefix caching ON for repeated prompt. Model: springboard-v1-int8 (post-quant), kernel set: default (auto).

olivia: Summary (excerpt):
- us-east H100 direct-pop: p50 48ms, p95 95ms
- us-east H100 edge-mux: p50 52ms, p95 110ms
- us-west A100 direct-pop: p50 55ms, p95 120ms
- us-west A100 edge-mux: p50 58ms, p95 160ms
- eu-west H100 direct-pop: p50 60ms, p95 110ms
- eu-west H100 edge-mux: p50 62ms, p95 190ms  <-- big tail

nina: Interesting — eu-west tail only spikes when edge-mux routes through proxy-pop-3. Did you see increased hop count or TLS renegotiation?

olivia: I pulled traces. edge-mux path in eu-west shows extra 2 network hops + 1 nginx proxy with 15-40ms per-request variation. KV cache hit rates are identical. No TLS renegos.

tomas: Could be kernel fallback on H100 under that traffic shape. When quantized kernels aren't selected, runtime falls back to slower int8 fallback path. Can you share runtime logs?

olivia: Pasting relevant runtime grep:
```
[2025-03-18 13:42:11] runtime: kernel_select: model=springboard-v1-int8, seq=512 -> selected_kernel=int8-opt-h100
[2025-03-18 13:43:05] runtime: kernel_select: model=springboard-v1-int8, seq=512 -> selected_kernel=fallback-generic
[2025-03-18 13:43:05] runtime: note: memory_pressure=false, batch_size=1
```

samir: That's the smoking gun. Why would it flip to fallback-generic intermittently? Memory fragmentation or transient occupancy?

tomas: Could be CUDA kernel timeout when proxy adds jitter to request arrivals — batching windows close differently. Try forcing kernel to int8-opt-h100 via runtime override and re-run edge-mux for eu-west for 15m. Also try enabling conservative batching (min-latency mode off).

olivia: Will run two quick canaries: (1) force-kernel=int8-opt-h100, (2) conservative-batching=true. Re-running now.

benchbot: Automated note: scheduled benchmark job qb-1749994321-run1 (eu-west, edge-mux, force-kernel) starting. Results will post when finished. :rocket:

deploy-bot: Canary env created: canary-euw-1749 — pinned nodes: 2xH100, runtime=23.4.0, monitoring hooks enabled.

nina: Also validate p95 breakdown by service: runtime CPU, grpc proxy, nginx, network. If runtime p95 stays low but overall p95 high, point to proxy.

olivia: Attached quick breakpoint from first 5 minutes: runtime p95 stayed ~98ms, nginx proxy p95 ~120ms, network tail contributed ~55ms on some traces. When kernel fallback occurred, runtime p95 jumped to ~180ms which explains worst-case tail.

samir: OK next steps: 1) run the two canaries (force-kernel / conservative-batching) 2) collect traceroutes for the edge-mux path 3) add a temporary bypass route to test direct-pop only 4) if kernel flips persist, open a runtime issue for kernel selector heuristics.

olivia: Canaries done — quick numbers from benchbot:
- force-kernel int8-opt-h100, eu-west edge-mux: p50 61ms, p95 105ms
- conservative-batching true, eu-west edge-mux: p50 64ms, p95 112ms
- direct-pop still wins: p95 ~98-105ms

tomas: Good sign — forcing kernel removed the big tail. That implies selector heuristic is over-eager under jitter. I'll file an RFC to adjust thresholds.

nina: For capacity sizing note: if we want p95<120ms under edge-mux for eu-west interactive, plan for 2.5x headroom on A100 and 1.8x on H100 when running int8. We'll include margin for edge variability.

olivia: Agreed. I'll update the onboarding doc with: kernel-override knob, recommended conservative-batching for EU edge-mux, and a routing checklist (bypass test + traceroute). Also adding a short HOWTO for evaluating p50/p95 contributions.

samir: Thanks — can you drop the trimmed bench artifacts (csv + flamegraph link)?

olivia: Dropped artifacts: https://s3.redwood-internal/springboard/1749994321/bench-results.csv and flame: https://grafana.redwood/s/prv/springboard-euw-flame

benchbot: Job qb-1749994321-run1 completed: summary uploaded.

olivia: I'll follow up tomorrow with the RFC link and a small script to replay the edge-mux jitter in a local harness. Thanks all :thumbsup:
